breach.name: UnderArmour
breach.title: Under Armour
breach.summary: In November 2025, the Everest ransomware group claimed Under Armour as a victim and attempted to extort a ransom, alleging they had obtained access to 343GB of data. In January 2026, customer data from the incident was published publicly on a popular hacking forum, including 72M email addresses. Many records also contained additional personal information such as names, dates of birth, genders…

fields.name: Dates of birth
fields.why: One of the three things call centres ask to verify identity, and it never changes.

fields.name: Geographic locations
fields.why: Where the account was used, which narrows a person down further than most people expect.

fields.name: Names
fields.why: Turns an anonymous address into an identified person, which is what makes targeted phishing possible.

fields.name: Purchases
fields.why: What was bought and when, detail that makes an impersonation convincing.

fields.name: Email addresses
fields.why: The address becomes a confirmed, active target, expect more phishing, better aimed.

fields.name: Genders
fields.why: Small on its own; useful to anyone assembling a fuller profile.

actions: Expect better-aimed phishing. A message that already knows your name and where you have an account is the whole point of a breach like this.
breach.scale_line: That is roughly everyone in the United Kingdom.
